title: Time-series schema: partitioned tables, partition maintenance, batched upsert writers
description: Migration 002 creating the §3.3 tables (candles_1m, candles_agg, mark_funding_1m, funding_settlements, open_interest_5m, long_short_5m, liquidations, calendar_events, collector_gaps) with the stated keys, CHECK constraints and monthly RANGE partitioning (funding_settlements and calendar_events unpartitioned). db/partitions.ts: pure function computing the partitions needed for [from, to] plus a service that creates the current month + 3 ahead on boot (before any collector starts) and daily, and on demand for any month the backfill touches. collectors/writers: one writer per table with batched INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (≤ 500 rows/statement), SQL built by pure functions with specs, and an integration spec against a real Postgres (skipped when DATABASE_URL is unset, as signal-server does). Liquidation side normalised to 'long'|'short' = the side liquidated; document the Binance ≤ 1 event/s/symbol undercount in the table comment. Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §3.1, §3.3, D6, D7, D12. Done when: migrations apply and undo; a spec proves a write into a month with no partition fails loudly and that maintenance creates it; writers are idempotent (re-writing the same batch changes nothing); row-count estimate in the README.

title: Binance USD-M perp collector: kline_1m, markPrice, forceOrder, funding settlements, gap repair
description: collectors/binance-perp using libs/binance-client: one combined-stream socket for <sym>@kline_1m of every universe symbol plus !markPrice@arr@1s and !forceOrder@arr. Closed 1m → candles_1m (with taker fields) through GapRepair per symbol (REST repair, gaps → collector_gaps). markPrice: keep the last message per symbol, write one mark_funding_1m row per symbol per minute boundary; when next_funding_time rolls over, fetch the settled rate (/fapi/v1/fundingRate limit=1) into funding_settlements and write the last prediction as a row stamped at the settlement second. forceOrder → liquidations. Boot: seed GapRepair from the last stored open_time per symbol and REST-fill to now before opening the socket. Dead-socket rule: no message for 90 s → reconnect; the 24 h server disconnect is an ordinary reconnect. DEGRADED MODE (design §16.1, ruling 2026-09-28 — the local network's fstream WS is mute): when the socket is mute (no data 30 s after open, or 90 s silence later) switch per stream to REST polling — klines /fapi/v1/klines?limit=2 every 3 s for the signal set and every 15 s for the rest (≈170 weight/min, stated in the header), mark/predicted funding via /fapi/v1/premiumIndex with no symbol (weight 10) once a minute, forceOrder has no REST equivalent and is recorded as an unrepaired gap; /health shows mode: degraded per stream; retry the socket every 5 min and return to WS on recovery. StreamRegistry (collectors/health) records last message per stream and feeds /health and the prom gauges of §6.1. State the REST weight per minute in the module header (design: ≈0.1 in steady state, 5 per repaired range). Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §4.1, §4.4, §6.1. Done when: mapper/sampling/rollover logic is pure and spec'd on recorded payload fixtures; a ≥ 30 min live run from a dev slot IN DEGRADED MODE shows continuous candles for all symbols and mark rows every minute (liquidations absent and declared in /health), a kill-and-restart produces a repaired gap in collector_gaps, and a spec covers the WS→degraded→WS transitions on fixtures; the WS-path live run happens on the Tokyo box as IB-026's first step, not here.

title: Binance OI and long/short 5 m poller with 30-day boot backfill
description: collectors/binance-perp/oi-ls.poller.ts: at every 5-minute boundary + 20 s call openInterestHist?period=5m&limit=1 and topLongShortPositionRatio, topLongShortAccountRatio, globalLongShortAccountRatio, takerlongshortRatio (period=5m, limit=1) for every universe symbol → open_interest_5m (oi_base, oi_quote from sumOpenInterestValue) and long_short_5m (kinds top_position, top_account, global_account, taker). Boot backfill: for each symbol whose last stored slot is older than 5 min, page the venue's 30-day window backward by endTime (500 rows/page; the endpoint returns the newest rows in [startTime,endTime], and startTime older than 30 days is rejected with code -1130 — see apps/signal-server/src/market-data/metrics/binance/binance-metrics.adapter.ts header). Weight: 5 calls × 30 symbols / 5 min = 30 weight/min (1.25 % of 2400) — state it in the module header and expose ib_binance_weight_used_1m from the X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M header. Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §4.1, §4.5. Done when: mappers spec'd on real payloads; a live run shows a complete 5 m grid for 1 h on all symbols; the backfill fills 30 days on a fresh database; missing slots land in collector_gaps.

title: Bybit collector: liquidations, mark/predicted funding, settled funding history
description: collectors/bybit: WS wss://stream.bybit.com/v5/public/linear subscribing allLiquidation.<symbol> for every symbol with bybit_linear (confirm the current topic name against Bybit v5 docs at build time; liquidation.<symbol> is deprecated) and tickers.<symbol> (markPrice, fundingRate, nextFundingTime); client ping every 20 s; reconnect with backoff; dead-socket rule as IB-005. tickers → mark_funding_1m once per minute for signal_set symbols, once per settlement for the rest (§3.3 volume rule); at settlement fetch /v5/market/funding/history (200/page) → funding_settlements, and on boot page back as far as the venue serves, recording the achieved depth in the module README. Done when: mapper specs on recorded payloads with the doc excerpt quoted in the mapper header; ≥ 30 min live run with liquidation and mark rows; funding history depth measured and written down; /health streams registered.

title: DevOps: EC2 t4g.small in ap-northeast-1 with docker compose, SSM secrets, daily pg_dump to S3, deploy path, Russian runbook
description: Provision per Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §7: one t4g.small (arm64) in ap-northeast-1, gp3 50 GB, no inbound ports (SSM Session Manager only), docker compose with postgres:16-alpine (data on EBS, shared_buffers 512MB) and insight-bot; secrets from SSM Parameter Store SecureString rendered to a root-only .env by the deploy step; daily pg_dump -Fc at 01:00 UTC to a versioned S3 bucket with 35-day lifecycle plus a documented restore drill; GitHub Actions job building the linux/arm64 image → ECR → ssm send-command docker compose pull && up -d; IaC (Terraform or CDK, your call) under infra/insight-bot/. FIRST action on the box: a connectivity probe opening Binance fstream, Binance spot, Bybit and OKX public WS and confirming messages within 30 s; a mute venue is escalated to the Tech Lead/Architect, not worked around. Runbook infra/insight-bot/RUNBOOK.md in plain Russian: deploy, restore, rotate a token, read /health, what a watchdog alert means. Cost target ≈ 20–25 USD/month. Done when: the instance runs IB-003's image with /health reachable via SSM port-forward, the probe results are recorded in the runbook, one backup exists in S3 and was restored once, and the deploy job has run end to end. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Dispatched in two parts: the venue connectivity probe and the IaC/workflow/RUNBOOK files may be written and reviewed now; NO AWS resource may be created, changed or destroyed (no terraform apply/CDK deploy, no bucket, instance, ECR repo or SSM parameter) and no AWS credentials requested or used until the user gives their go-ahead, which the Tech Lead has asked for. The deploy step also waits for IB-003 to merge. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Part 1 (probe + all files) merged at 7302c03. Part 2 (the AWS apply, SSM parameters, box probe, deploy, restore drill) is BLOCKED on the user's go-ahead plus the bucket name and the OIDC decision; nothing in AWS until then. IB-003 must be merged before the deploy step. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28, user decisions: reports/zinc-raven-ib013-user-decisions.md] Part 2 unblocked with conditions. (a) HARD CAP 20 USD/month for everything including the public IPv4 charge, EBS, S3 and snapshots; the earlier 22-24 estimate does not fit, so re-plan with a line-by-line monthly cost table in the review, plus an AWS Budgets alert at 18 USD. Levers named by the user: a smaller gp3 disk, no ECR (build on the box or pull from GHCR), no ALB/NAT, t4g.micro + swap if t4g.small does not fit. (b) Backup bucket vb-insight-bot-backups-apne1 in ap-northeast-1; if the name is taken add a short suffix without asking. (c) Credentials: no keys in any .env and agents never read .env. dev-3 writes a least-privilege PROVISIONING policy JSON (EC2/EBS, that one S3 bucket, SSM parameters, the instance IAM role, Budgets; region-scoped); the user creates the IAM user, attaches it and runs `aws configure --profile insight-bot` themselves; dev-3 uses AWS_PROFILE=insight-bot, never prints keys, and the user can deactivate those keys after provisioning. At runtime the box uses an instance role only (S3 backup + SSM read), no keys on the box. Deploy: GitHub OIDC if the repo's Actions are used, else SSM Run Command or SSH from the user's machine - dev-3 picks one and says why. (d) Hand the user the exact steps in plain Russian. Apply only once the profile exists, and report each step. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Paused by the user: no new assignments and no merges until the pause is lifted; work in progress stays on its branch as it is. DEFERRED by the user 2026-10-12: the dashboard stream continues without it. The only thing it waits on is the user re-pasting `infra/insight-bot/iam/provisioner-policy.json` into the `insight-bot-provisioner` policy in the console - verified still unpasted on 2026-10-12 (`s3:GetBucketPolicy` denied, no EC2 instance in ap-northeast-1, 5 of 12 resources exist, all free, $0.27 spend). Not to be chased. No dashboard task depends on it. STATE AT RISK, recorded 2026-10-12 (dev-3): the only tofu state for the 5 live resources is a GITIGNORED file inside dev-3's worktree (infra/insight-bot/terraform/terraform.tfstate); dev-3 copied it, with terraform.tfvars, to ~/.claude/jobs/0028abca/tmp/reports/ib-013-state-backup/ (checked to be outside any git repo, because tfvars carries the user's e-mail). A backup is not a fix, so the identifiers go HERE in plain text, because identifiers are the truth and state is only a convenience: aws_iam_role.instance, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm_core, aws_iam_instance_profile.insight_bot, aws_security_group.insight_bot = sg-01cb82a6578c17200, aws_s3_bucket.backups = vb-insight-bot-backups-apne1 (ap-northeast-1, empty). All five cost zero, so there is no bill pressure. Whoever resumes: do not delete that worktree without taking the state file, or decide instead to delete these five by hand and start clean - either is fine, losing the state by accident is not. An S3 remote backend is the real fix and is deliberately out of scope until the stack is live. BACKUP VERIFICATION, required before the daily pg_dump-to-S3 job can be called done (learned 2026-10-12 from dev-2's restore rehearsal on the local tape, IB-041): the job dumps PARTITIONED tables, so it must use `--load-via-partition-root` or a restore cannot place rows (there is deliberately no DEFAULT partition, so it fails loudly instead of mis-filing). And the job's integrity check must verify CONTENT, not the container: `--table=<parent>` silently produces an empty dump that `gzip -t` passes, so a green daily backup can mean an empty file. Check a row count or a digest against the source and alarm on it; a backup nobody has restored is not a backup, so the restore side gets rehearsed once on the box too. | ПЕРЕСМОТРЕНО 2026-10-31 (Архитектор): часть 2 переписана как IB-073 (принять пять ресурсов import-блоками в новое состояние в S3, затем apply). Эту задачу закрыть как заменённую; статус — Техлиду.

title: Derive 15m/1h/4h/1d candles_agg from 1m on close and over history
description: derive/: pure fold of 1m rows into a tf bucket (OHLC, volume, quote_volume, trades, taker fields summed, bars count, complete flag) with specs; a job driven by a BarClock (UTC minute + 5 s grace) writing the just-closed bucket for every tf, and a `npm run derive -- --from --to` command over history (idempotent upsert). Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §8.1, D4. Done when: derived 4h bars for a stored month equal Binance's native 4h klines fetched once for the check (OHLCV within float tolerance; documented); incomplete buckets are marked; live run shows buckets appearing within 10 s of close. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Dispatched ahead of the rest of stage 1 because the dashboard already serves WebTimeframe values that resolve to candles_agg, and because insight_dev1 and insight_dev3 hold the IB-012 archive (20.4M 1m candles) that the done-line's check against Binance native 4h needs. IB-031's client half will read these rows, so a derived bar that disagrees with the venue is a visible wrong number on a chart, not just a row in a table. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Before writing a migration, ls apps/insight-bot/migrations and take the next free number: versions are first-come, and two migrations sharing one version makes postgrator refuse to run AT ALL (it fails every DB suite, not just yours - it cost 6 suites / 52 tests in IB-036).

title: Feature engine: the fixed feature frame at 15m and 4h closes
description: features/: feature-keys.ts fixing the §8.2 key set and frame_version; pure calculators per group (funding percentiles per venue and extreme-venue counts, OI deltas and 7-day-high flag, L/S percentiles, spot/perp CVD windows and slopes from candles_1m taker fields, Wilder ATR(14) 1h/4h/1d from candles_agg, swing/failed-high/impulse-low structure from 15m bars, liquidation sums and 30-day log1p z-scores (null until 14 days of history), price context, the P4 label of §9.2); a FeaturePass service running at every 15m and 4h close + 15 s grace that reads ONLY candles_agg buckets with complete=true (design §8.1 as amended by §16.10): if the closing bucket, any bucket inside a feature's window, or the OI slot is incomplete at the grace, re-check at +30 s and +60 s, then write the frame with complete=false and incomplete_reason; when IB-014's heal pass completes the bucket later, recompute that frame idempotently on (symbol, tf, close_time) and emit a 'frame-recomputed' event the runner (IB-017) consumes once; a frame with complete=false can never arm or trigger a playbook (spec this), writing feature_frames. Symbols with no spot get null CVD, never zero. Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §8.1, §8.2, §9.2. Done when: every calculator has specs on hand-built fixtures with worked numbers; a `npm run features -- --from --to` command recomputes frames over stored history (for the later backtest runner); live frames appear for the signal set within 30 s of each close. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Before writing a migration, ls apps/insight-bot/migrations and take the next free number: versions are first-come, and two migrations sharing one version makes postgrator refuse to run AT ALL (it fails every DB suite, not just yours - it cost 6 suites / 52 tests in IB-036). [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] The Architect's §16.10 ruling is a hard requirement of this task, not a nicety: the feature pass reads only complete=true buckets, re-checks at +30/+60 s, writes complete=false with a reason rather than computing on short input, recomputes when the bucket heals, and an INCOMPLETE FRAME CAN NEVER ARM OR TRIGGER. IB-014's heal pass is the precedent for the mechanics. Spec the refusal path as carefully as the happy one: a frame built on a short bar feeds an arming decision, not a chart. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Paused by the user: no new assignments and no merges until the pause is lifted; work in progress stays on its branch as it is. UNBLOCKED 2026-10-12: the status was stale - both dependencies (IB-014 derive, IB-007 OI/long-short poller) have been merged for some time. Re-assigned from dev-3 to dev-2, who spent 2026-10-12 finding and fixing four separate cases of a confidently wrong number (IB-BUG-011's venue join, IB-038's norm basis, IB-042's discarded count, IB-043's month labels); the feature frame is where that instinct is worth the most, because a feature that is quietly wrong does not look wrong anywhere - it just moves a signal. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT 2026-10-12, ruled while deciding IB-016's history source: the feature pass needs a HISTORY MODE - run over past closes from raw data under the frame's own rules, the way IB-014's derive job takes --from --to. Reason: IB-016's vol and leverage axes read their histories from STORED FRAMES rather than raw tables, because an axis reading raw tables can disagree with the frame it is attached to - two numbers about one instant computed under different completeness decisions, with nothing to say which is right. Stored frames alone would mean both axes refuse everywhere for about thirty days while history accrues; a backfill gives consistency AND answers immediately. Cheap to design in now, expensive to bolt on, same argument as putting the EMA keys in while WEB_FRAME_VERSION is still 1.

title: Regime context axes (trend, vol, leverage, event window) as stored context
description: regime/: compute per frame trend (EMA50 4h slope + price vs EMA200 1d), vol (ATR(14) 4h percentile over 90 days: <30/30–80/>80), leverage (OI percentile over 90 days combined with the 3-day mean funding sign), event_window (EVENT_RISK inside ±60 min of a high-impact USD calendar_events row), plus a market-scope row from BTC. Written to regime_context; exposed to the engine ONLY through the context_gate mechanism of IB-017 and the global EVENT_RISK veto — no other code path may read regime_context in a playbook (add a lint/spec guard: playbooks/ must not import regime/). Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §8.3, D9. Done when: calculators spec'd; a guard spec fails if playbooks/ imports regime/; context visible in a debug REST endpoint GET /debug/context/:symbol (dev only). [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Before writing a migration, ls apps/insight-bot/migrations and take the next free number: versions are first-come, and two migrations sharing one version makes postgrator refuse to run AT ALL (it fails every DB suite, not just yours - it cost 6 suites / 52 tests in IB-036). MIGRATION NUMBER ALLOCATION, from 2026-10-12: numbers are allocated by the Tech Lead on request and recorded here, because three collisions happened in one day - IB-027's 009 against a merged 009/010, then IB-027's 011 against IB-015's unmerged 011, then IB-016 about to take 013 which IB-028 already holds on ib-dex-snapshots. The cause is structural, not carelessness: `ls apps/insight-bot/migrations` on master shows 011 as the highest, so the next free number LOOKS like 012 while two unmerged branches already hold 012 and 013. Checking every ref works but decays between uses. Current ledger: 001-011 merged; 012 = IB-027 news (dev-3, ib-news-ingest); 013 = IB-028 dex snapshots (dev-3, ib-dex-snapshots); 014 = IB-016 regime storage (dev-1). Ask before taking the next one. MIGRATION RENUMBER 2026-10-12: 014 -> 017 (no files created yet, so this costs nothing). MIGRATION LEDGER CORRECTED 2026-10-12, after a sequencing error of mine. I allocated 012/013/014/015 in order and then let 015 merge before 013 and 014 existed, so master now holds 001-012 and 015 with a hole at 013/014. Allocating numbers in order does NOT prevent the skip hazard if merges happen out of order: postgrator runs only versions ABOVE the current one, so any database migrated from master now reaches 15 and would never apply a 013 or 014 landing later. title: Playbook engine: Playbook port, state machine, twin-arm runner, versioned config, signals table
description: playbooks/: the Playbook interface of §8.4 (pure evaluate(input) → output), SetupState machine IDLE→ARMED→TRIGGERED→CLOSED with armed_ttl_bars expiry and cooldown check, playbook_config loading (active = highest version with status ≠ off; seed v1 from config/playbooks.yaml by migration), and the runner: for each (playbook, symbol ∈ signal_set) on that playbook's tf close, evaluate arm 'gated' (context_gate applied if declared: exactly one {observable, op, value} over a regime axis or a feature key) and arm 'unconditional' (always shadow) with identical params; persist playbook_state; on 'triggered' insert a signals row (UNIQUE (playbook, symbol, trigger_ts, arm)) with setup, feature_snapshot (the full frame), regime, conditions; status_at_signal recorded. Migration 003 for §3.4 tables. A fixture playbook in specs proves the state transitions, TTL, twin arms and idempotent re-run. Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §8.3, §8.4, D9, D10, D12. Done when: specs above green; running the runner twice over the same frames inserts nothing new; a config version bump is a new row and the runner picks it up without restart. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Before writing a migration, ls apps/insight-bot/migrations and take the next free number: versions are first-come, and two migrations sharing one version makes postgrator refuse to run AT ALL (it fails every DB suite, not just yours - it cost 6 suites / 52 tests in IB-036). BINDING RULING 2026-10-12 (from dev-1's IB-016 work): the gate's calendar check is COVERAGE OF THE WINDOW BEING ASKED ABOUT - is there calendar data spanning this frame's +/-60 minutes - and NEVER non-emptiness. Measured proof that this is not hypothetical: on 2026-10-12 calendar_events held 256 rows with events to 2026-10-09 and a last fetched_at of 2026-10-07 13:52 local (it stopped when the user had the interim collector stopped, so it is switched off rather than broken). A wiring that set calendarLoaded = (rows exist) would have found those rows and reported CLEAR on every frame for nine days - wrong in the only direction that costs money. A stale table has rows and no coverage, which is the same pair of facts IB-BUG-010 separated for collectors: not_recorded is not no_events. Also ruled for this task: when the calendar cannot be shown covered the gate fails CLOSED, under the reason `calendar_unknown` and never `EVENT_RISK`, counted separately, so a dead collector can never masquerade as a busy news week. DISPATCHED 2026-10-12 to dev-2, who built the frame contract and therefore knows what a refusal means. Carried requirements from the day's rulings: arming is PER KEY via canArm against a named required-key list, never off the `complete` flag; a playbook must refuse a MIXED set - assertSingleComputedMode and assertSingleRevisionPerClose exist for this, and liveRevisions() is the read a live arm uses so a backfilled amendment can never inform a decision that was made before it existed; the calendar check is coverage of the asked-about window, never non-emptiness, and an unshowable calendar fails CLOSED under its own reason `calendar_unknown`, counted separately, never `EVENT_RISK`. MIGRATION 015 allocated to this task 2026-10-12 (ledger: 001-011 merged, 012 news dev-3, 013 dex dev-3, 014 regime dev-1, 015 playbook/signals dev-2). RULED 2026-10-12 on dev-2's proposal: an arm's evaluation window must be CONTIGUOUSLY EVALUABLE IN THE ARM'S OWN MODE, and `expired_unevaluable` is a distinct reason counted apart from an honest expiry - declaring 'expired without trigger' when some closes in the window were never evaluated asserts something we did not see. It composes with computed_mode for free because a live arm reads liveRevisions only. ADDED by the Tech Lead: the timestamp half is the sharper one. A trigger found after a hole must carry THE CLOSE IT ACTUALLY FIRED AT and, separately, when we evaluated it - two facts, two fields, exactly as news carries the publisher's date beside our first-seen instant and the signed skew between them. Stamping a 45-minute-old trigger with today's timestamp and today's price is the news anchor-skew defect arriving in the signals path, where it costs money rather than a correlation. Beyond a stated bound the two diverging is not a signal to send: it is a late detection, and it must be refused and counted as one rather than delivered. CLARIFIED 2026-10-12: TWO things share the word 'gate' and they are ruled differently. (a) The 8.5 DELIVERY gate - status, dedupe, cooldown, budget, correlation, sizing, which is IB-020 - is evaluated at BOTH arm and trigger, with budget/correlation/sizing authoritative at trigger because they are properties of the delivery moment; a budget gated only at arm is a number we printed rather than kept, and a suppressed trigger is recorded with its reason rather than dropped. (b) D9's per-playbook CONTEXT GATE - the single declared observable defining the gated arm - is ARM-TIME ONLY, per dev-2's recommendation. The load-bearing reason is experimental, not stylistic: the twin-arm design exists to measure whether the gate adds value, which requires the gated arm to be a clean SUBSET of the unconditional arm. If the context gate could also kill armed setups, the gated arm becomes a different process and any difference in outcome conflates 'the gate filtered entries' with 'the gate exited early', so the comparison D9 asks for could not be attributed. Secondary reason, also right: a setup already has invalidation[] for conditions changing after arming, and two mechanisms ending a setup means a playbook author cannot tell which one did. ADDED by the Tech Lead: when a context gate's observable is UNAVAILABLE at arm time (gate_axis_unavailable), the gated arm not arming must be counted SEPARATELY from the gate genuinely not passing - otherwise the gate's measured value is contaminated by our own outages and we would conclude 'the gate costs performance' when the truth is 'we were blind for part of the window'. The twin-arm comparison must be able to exclude periods where the gated arm could not be evaluated at all. RULED YES 2026-10-12 on the per-close evaluation record: one audit row per (playbook, symbol, arm, close_time) in migration 015 beside signals, recording evaluated-and-armed, evaluated-and-did-not, or refused-with-which-reason. dev-2 is right that it cannot live on the signal row, because a gated arm that never armed produces no signal, so the absence of a row is ambiguous between 'evaluated and declined' and 'could not evaluate' - the exact ambiguity every ruling today has been about. It also yields the insufficient_features and blind_while_armed counters from one place instead of three. Cost measured rather than guessed: P3 at 15m over 3 symbols x 2 arms x 96 closes = 576 rows/day, about 210k/year, partitioned on close_time. WHY RECORD RATHER THAN DERIVE, since evaluability is in principle recomputable from the stored frame plus the playbook's key list: a derivation is a RECONSTRUCTION, and today's computed_mode ruling exists precisely because a later recomputation is not what happened at the time - the code, the config version and the healed buckets all differ. Deriving evaluability after the fact is computing it in backfill mode and calling it history. ADDED: the audit row carries the PLAYBOOK VERSION, because the required-key list and the gate observable are versioned config and 'did not arm' is meaningless without the rules it did not arm under; and it carries source_mode like signals, so a backtest's audit rows can never be mixed with live ones. MODE-IN-KEY RULE, generalised 2026-10-12 after the THIRD instance was found by implementing rather than designing: frames needed computed_mode per revision, signals and the per-close audit needed source_mode, and then playbook_state needed it too - and that one is the worst of the three, because playbook_state is keyed per playbook x symbol x arm, so a backtest would not merely add a duplicate row, it would OVERWRITE the state the live engine is currently holding. The rule to apply without rediscovering it: when two runners can execute the same code over different time domains, EVERY table either carries the mode in its key or must be provably single-writer. FORWARD CATCH, before the fourth instance costs anything: `alert_budget` must carry the mode when it is created. A backtest spending the live daily budget would SUPPRESS REAL SIGNALS to the user - the only failure in this chain that silently withholds something the user was owed rather than adding something wrong. Same for deliveries and user_actions, which are per-user state a backtest must never touch. CONFIG RULINGS 2026-10-12, all three in dev-2's favour against the task's own wording. (1) The task said active = highest version with status != off, which read literally makes `off` a REVERT switch rather than a kill switch: setting the newest version off falls back to the previous one and silently re-activates it, so an admin typing /playbook P3 off during a problem watches signals continue, concludes the command is broken, and the playbook trades on older less-tested thresholds nobody chose. A kill switch that appears not to work is worse than none, because the operator debugs the switch during the incident. CORRECT SEMANTICS: the newest version IS the configuration and its status decides whether it runs. Revert must be an explicit new version carrying the old values, never an implicit fallback, because a fallback records nothing; and /playbook status prints the active version AND its status so an operator reads 'v7, off' rather than inferring from an absence of signals. (2) threshold vs value: accept both spellings on read, hard error on absence, but NORMALISE ON WRITE to 8.3's `value` and document the reader's leniency as a migration aid with its reason, so it can be deleted once no row uses the old name instead of surviving as a feature. (3) A malformed or two-gate context_gate THROWS at load rather than being ignored, and dev-2's reason is the one to keep: ignoring it would run a playbook the operator believes is gated while the twin-arm comparison quietly compares an arm against itself - not a crash and not a wrong number but a NULL RESULT IN AN EXPERIMENT, which would be believed and used to discredit a true idea with evidence we manufactured.

Design: architecture/insight-bot-system-design.md §10, §13 p.4. Done when: 24 h of snapshots across the four networks; rate-limit accounting in the README; specs for mappers and the snapshot cadence. [Tech Lead, 2026-09-28] Before writing a migration, ls apps/insight-bot/migrations and take the next free number: versions are first-come, and two migrations sharing one version makes postgrator refuse to run AT ALL (it fails every DB suite, not just yours - it cost 6 suites / 52 tests in IB-036). DISPATCHED 2026-10-12. Added at dispatch: a live pass against all four real APIs is a MERGE PREREQUISITE, not a follow-up (IB-027's live pass found four findings in one run, one of which would have merged); every parser and detector carries a positive control fixture that must fire (three of 2026-10-12's silent zeros had never worked at all); and an absent value is never zero - a missing liquidity reading, an unanswered GoPlus query or an omitted holder count must each be distinguishable from a measured zero. Rate limits are to be MEASURED under AGENTS.md's repetition rule, not quoted, with the request rate per minute of every added loop stated in the README. MIGRATION RENUMBER 2026-10-12: 013 -> 016. MIGRATION LEDGER CORRECTED 2026-10-12, after a sequencing error of mine. I allocated 012/013/014/015 in order and then let 015 merge before 013 and 014 existed, so master now holds 001-012 and 015 with a hole at 013/014. Allocating numbers in order does NOT prevent the skip hazard if merges happen out of order: postgrator runs only versions ABOVE the current one, so any database migrated from master now reaches 15 and would never apply a 013 or 014 landing later. No slot database is above 12, so nothing is damaged - the trap was live for the next person to migrate, not for anyone yet. FIX: the unmerged branches move ABOVE the highest number on master. dev-3's dex snapshots 013 -> 016; dev-1's regime storage 014 -> 017. The hole at 013/014 becomes permanent and harmless, because a number no migration will ever claim cannot be skipped. THE REAL INVARIANT, which the planned guard must assert instead of strict contiguity: no duplicate versions, AND no new migration numbered at or below the highest version already on master. Strict contiguity cannot be restored - 015 is merged - and is not the property that matters; the property that matters is that a number can never appear below a version some database has already passed. PRESENCE CONTRACT RULED 2026-10-13, replacing the Tech Lead's earlier requirement, which rested on a false premise about the API. Measured: GoPlus EVM shares only 5 of 29 field names between two real responses, so the field set varies per token by design and 'this field vanished from the API' is NOT detectable per response - the signal does not exist in the data. dev-3's replacement is approved and is better: an always-field now REPORTS (row kept, ERROR logged, the name recorded in absent_fields) and only a payload with no distinctive field at all throws, so the throw is reserved for 'this is not the API we think it is'. REQUIRED CONSEQUENCE: with a per-token-variable field set, a shape change is detectable only IN THE AGGREGATE, so absent_fields must be consumed as a RATE - field presence per chain family over time, on the coverage or audit surface - or it is another honesty column with no consumer. ALSO: dev-3 corrected two of their own earlier claims, one of which the Tech Lead had accepted and endorsed into a schema comment - is_honeypot and is_proxy DO exist. The comment must be corrected, not only the report, because the artefact is what the next reader believes. AND a measured exception worth recording: AGENTS.md exempts payload SHAPES from the repetition rule on the grounds that a shape does not drift and a fixture catches it immediately; GoPlus falsifies that premise for itself, since its shape varies per token, so for this API shapes need the repetition rule too and a two-response sample is not a sample. LEDGER CORRECTED 2026-10-13: I double-promised 017 - reserved for IB-016's regime storage, then given to IB-053 - by allocating from memory after saying the ledger was a record and not an allocator. dev-1 caught it. NO NUMBER IS RESERVED FOR ANYONE. Under the merge-time rule the number is taken immediately before the fast-forward and must equal master_highest + 1, enforced by the uniqueness and burned-gap guards; a reservation is the thing that rule abolished, and holding one in my head is how 012-015 got burned in the first place. The ledger records USED and BURNED only: used 001-012 and 015-016; burned 013 and 014. Whoever merges next takes 017, whoever merges after that takes 018.

title: insight-bot no longer boots without DATABASE_URL: CalendarModule imports WritersModule unconditionally
description: Found by dev-3 while rebasing IB-005 over IB-010 (reports/dev3-IB-005-rebase.md §2). IB-003's rule (design §2.1 and its done-line) is that DATABASE_URL has no default and the app still boots and serves /health and /metrics without one; IB-004's writers.module.ts is deliberately kept out of AppModule for exactly that reason. IB-010's src/collectors/calendar/calendar.module.ts imports WritersModule unconditionally, and Writers throws when DB is null, so on current master the process exits at boot with 'Writers: no database' and /health is unreachable (curl HTTP 000). CALENDAR_ENABLED=false does not help: the module is still imported. Reproduced by dev-3 on master + IB-005. Fix: make CalendarModule a dynamic module in the shape of CollectorsModule.register() - no Writers, no poller and a WARN line when DATABASE_URL is unset, unchanged behaviour when it is set. Done when: a spec boots the AppModule without DATABASE_URL and gets 200 on /health and /metrics (the IB-003 rule, now guarded by a test so it cannot regress again), the calendar specs stay green, and a real no-DB boot is shown in the report.

title: Monthly partition bounds are bare date literals, so they land in the DB session's timezone: the first hours of every UTC month have no partition
description: Found by dev-3 during IB-012 (reports/dev3-partition-tz-bug.md). apps/insight-bot/src/db/partitions.ts buildCreatePartition emits FOR VALUES FROM ('2026-09-01') TO ('2026-10-01'); the partition keys are timestamptz, so Postgres resolves the bare literals in the DATABASE SESSION's timezone. On a US/Pacific session (this machine's local Postgres: SHOW timezone = US/Pacific) every monthly partition is shifted 7 h, so 00:00-07:00 UTC on the 1st of each month falls in no partition and the write fails outright with 'no partition of relation ... found for row'. monthOf() is correctly UTC; only the SQL literal is wrong. Masked so far because the collectors have only written mid-month, and a UTC Postgres (the box's docker-compose) hides it entirely - so it would surface first on a non-UTC database or across a DST change. Fix: pin both bounds as '<date> 00:00:00+00', with a spec asserting the emitted SQL carries the offset, plus a spec (or integration check) that a row at 00:30 UTC on the 1st lands in that month's partition on a non-UTC session. Existing slot databases keep their skewed partitions: they must be dropped and recreated (document the exact steps in the insight-bot README so dev-1, dev-2 and the Tester do not each lose an hour). P0 because the next UTC month boundary is 2026-10-01. dev-3 already has the one-line fix in the ib-historical-backfill branch; land it on its own branch first so everyone can rebase onto it.

title: Админ: страница участников (список, отключить/включить, приглашение) и настройки участника на сайте (язык, напоминания календаря)
description:
ПЕРЕПИСАНО 2026-11-04 (Архитектор, по просьбе Техлида). Прежний текст просил депозит, risk_pct, daily_loss_limit и dex_alerts. Их удалил WD-013, а «следующий алерт Telegram с этим размером» больше не существует. Ниже — то, что осталось осмысленным. История — в git. Новых колонок и миграций нет: users.disabled, users.lang и users.calendar_alerts уже есть (005, 019). Зачем задача: заблокировать участника сейчас можно только SQL-запросом, а с платной подпиской это нужно владельцу из интерфейса.
СЕРВЕР (admin — по роли, как у IB-075; участник получает 403):
(1) GET /api/web/admin/members: id, имя и username в Telegram, login (null, если пароль не установлен), role, disabled, дата появления, последний успешный вход (из web_login_events), число активных сессий. Тот же список, что у /users в боте, — общий метод UsersService, а не второй SQL.
(2) POST /api/web/admin/invites: тот же сервис, что у /invite в боте. Ссылка показывается один раз и не хранится в ответах списка.
(3) POST /api/web/admin/members/:id/disable и /enable. disable ставит users.disabled=true и в той же транзакции удаляет все web_sessions участника; бот уже отвечает отключённому как не-участнику (bot-handlers). Отказ 409: отключить себя и отключить последнего активного админа. enable только снимает флаг; пароль остаётся прежним. Каждое действие — строка в логе с id админа.
(4) GET/PATCH /api/web/me/settings: { lang: 'ru'|'en', calendarAlerts: boolean } через UsersService.updateSettings и ТЕ ЖЕ парсеры, что у /lang и /calendar в боте. Спека паритета: одно и то же значение принимается или отклоняется одинаково обоими путями. Другие поля PATCH отклоняет (strict schema), а не игнорирует.
Контракты — первым коммитом в libs/contracts/src/insight/ с префиксом Web (правило IB-029).
КЛИЕНТ:
(5) /admin/members (только админ, пункт навигации рядом с журналом входов): таблица участников, на 390 px прокручивается в своём контейнере; кнопки «Отключить» / «Включить» с подтверждением; «Создать приглашение» показывает ссылку один раз с кнопкой копирования.
(6) Страница аккаунта (/account) получает раздел «Настройки»: язык и напоминания календаря в Telegram (решение владельца 2026-11-04: напоминания остаются). Смена языка сразу переключает интерфейс — I18nService уже берёт язык из /auth/me — и ответы бота.
ГОТОВО, когда: спеки паритета с ботом для lang и calendar; спеки отказов 409; интеграционная спека против Postgres слота — disable удаляет сессии, и следующий запрос этой сессии получает 401; вживую на слоте — второй аккаунт входит, админ его отключает, вкладка второго аккаунта при следующем действии оказывается на /login, а /start в боте отвечает как не-участнику; включить снова → вход тем же паролем. Скриншоты обеих страниц на 390 px и на десктопе. Правила компонентов AGENTS.md; i18n en/ru/keys с паритетом; npm test из apps/chart-client — оба проекта, числа jest и sha. Миграций нет, а если окажутся нужны — номер брать следующий свободный по ВСЕМ ref'ам.

title: symbols.coingecko_id was never created by any migration: the app does not boot at all, on a fresh database or an upgraded one
description: Found by dev-1 starting IB-037 (report in that branch). IB-031's migration 008 dropped symbols.coingecko_id on the understanding that IB-036's 007 declared it; 007 only MENTIONS it in a comment on market_cap_coin.coin, so nothing ever created the column. db/universe-sync.ts inserts into it on every boot, so boot-time universe sync failed with 'column coingecko_id of relation symbols does not exist' and the process died BEFORE listening: /health unreachable, symbols empty. Reproduces on a fresh database as well as migrated-in-place, so the Tokyo box would not have come up on day one. It survived CI because universe-sync.spec drives a FAKE database and only asserts that the INSERT names the column, never that a real schema has one. Fix: migration 009 adds the column (008 is taken; numbers are first-come), plus test/db/universe-sync.integration.spec.ts against a real schema with symbols already present (the second-boot case), control-checked so all five specs fail without 009. Lesson to carry: a spec that fakes the database cannot see a schema drift, so anything writing a column needs one integration spec against the real schema.

title: The one-shot 365-day coin backfill starves the forward-only /global poll: market_cap_global collected 1 row in 20 minutes
description: Observed on the coordinator's interim run (:3005, insight_coord, 2026-09-28 21:40-22:00Z, log /tmp/ib-coord.log). On a fresh database the IB-036 one-shot backfill fetches 365 days for 20 coins at the measured keyless rate (~2-3 req/min), which takes ~10 minutes and holds the shared CoinGecko IP allowance the whole time. The forward-only /global poll shares that allowance, so it got 1 row (21:33) and none after: its calls lose to the backfill's retries and its 10-minute slot advances only on success. The watchdog correctly raised 'Поток context:market-cap-global молчит 4 мин' (which would have gone to the service chat had a token existed), so the symptom is visible rather than silent - the defect is the starvation, not the reporting. Why it matters: market_cap_global is the one context series with NO history endpoint, so every slot lost here is lost for good, and the Tokyo box's first boot is exactly this shape (fresh database, backfill running, forward-only poll starved). Proposed fix for when the pause lifts: give the forward-only /global poll priority over the one-shot backfills - either run the backfills after the first successful /global sample, or share one scheduler that reserves a slot for /global every 10 minutes and lets the backfill use whatever is left. Do not raise the rate: it was measured. Done when: on a fresh database the backfill still completes AND /global collects a sample every 10 minutes throughout, shown by timestamps over at least 30 minutes. LESSON recorded 2026-10-12, from dev-1's failure-path capture on the live rig: the first fix created the MIRROR of the bug it fixed. Giving the forward-only /global poll priority made concurrent /global polls STACK under a 429, and the backfill then got 0 coins in 2 minutes - starvation in the opposite direction, invisible on the success path. Generalisable: a fix that reprioritises two consumers of ONE shared budget must be tested for starvation in BOTH directions, and only the failure path shows the second one. The Tech Lead asked for the failure capture on the rig that was already up rather than accepting the success path plus an injected-clock spec; that request is what found both defects. Second defect from the same capture: fetched_at recorded poll START rather than arrival, which under retries can be minutes early - and fetched_at is what IB-037's market cards render as «на {when} UTC», so the card was claiming a measurement instant earlier than the measurement. MERGED e53d2c1 2026-10-12 (approved as 0ffb91b; equivalence confirmed by `git range-diff 84ecb67..0ffb91b 3e91776..e53d2c1` reporting '=' on both commits, after dev-1 self-corrected their own `git diff` check, which compared across different bases and so showed 16 unrelated files). BLAST RADIUS, recorded here because it did not reach the commit message and history is not being rewritten to tidy that: the fetched_at fix matters for DIAGNOSTICS and gap detection, NOT for the user-facing card. The dashboard reads `ts`, and collectors/context/mappers.ts:64 stamps `ts` with CoinGecko's own `updated_at`, so «на {when} UTC» is the venue's measurement instant - better than either poll-start or arrival - and the defect never reached a number a user sees. 710 rows checked on insight_dev1, 0 with the impossible ordering. Boot evidence on a fresh database: the first CoinGecko request of the process was /global, sampled with zero coins fetched yet, which is the whole fix in one observation.

title: provisioner-policy.json names Budgets API actions that do not exist as IAM actions, and is missing S3 read actions terraform plan needs
description: The user hit this creating the IAM user from infra/insight-bot/iam/provisioner-policy.json (e062561): the AWS console rejects the policy with 'The action budgets:DescribeBudgets / CreateBudget / DeleteBudget does not exist'. Those are Budgets API names; the IAM actions are only budgets:ViewBudget (read) and budgets:ModifyBudget (create/update/delete), and Terraform's aws_budgets_budget needs just those two since budgets.tf sets no tags. Fix: ReadOnlyDiscovery drops budgets:DescribeBudgets and keeps budgets:ViewBudget; TheCostGuard's Action becomes [budgets:ViewBudget, budgets:ModifyBudget] with Resource unchanged. THE USER HAS ALREADY APPLIED THIS BY HAND IN THE CONSOLE, so the repo file must be brought in line with what is now in AWS, not the other way round. Second, likely failure at terraform plan rather than in the console: aws_s3_bucket's read refreshes many sub-resources (GetBucketPolicy, GetBucketAcl, GetBucketCORS, GetBucketWebsite, GetAccelerateConfiguration, GetBucketRequestPayment, GetBucketLogging, GetReplicationConfiguration, GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration, GetBucketOwnershipControls, GetLifecycleConfiguration) and most are absent from BackupBucketOnly, so plan/apply would hit AccessDenied and the user would have to edit the policy a second time; add the ones the provider version in use actually calls, scoped to the same bucket ARN. Validate the WHOLE policy before handing it back - IAM Access Analyzer validate-policy, or every action checked against the Service Authorization Reference - so the user edits it at most once more. Done when: every action in the file exists as an IAM action (evidence of the validation in the report), the repo file matches what the user has in the console plus the S3 reads, and the RUNBOOK/SETUP-RU text still matches the file.

title: Liquidations at a glance: «Ликвидации сейчас» card, «Где ликвидируют» table, «Крупные ликвидации» feed, one overview endpoint
description: User request 2026-10-07 (reports/zinc-raven-liquidations-visual.md): liquidations are not a chart. Server: GET /api/web/liquidations/overview?symbols=top20&feed_min_usd=… per Design: architecture/insight-bot-web-dashboard.md §12.3 — for 1 h / 4 h / 24 h market-wide and per top-20 coin: USD long, short, total and «× от нормы» (§12.2: trailing-W sum ÷ the 30-day median of consecutive boundary-aligned W-window sums, per side and total, over the venues present in the window, null until 7 days of history), the newest N events above the threshold (time, coin, side, USD, price, venue), and venues {present, missing}; one SQL pass per window, 15 s server-side cache, specs on a synthetic 30-day tape (including the venue-set rule: a venue joining later must not fake a spike); Web-prefixed zod contracts. Client, landing page: the «Ликвидации сейчас» card (per window: total USD, one horizontal long|short bar in the palette colours with both amounts, the ratio colour-escalated < 1.5 / 1.5–3 / ≥ 3, one plain line «сейчас выносят лонги» / «выносят шорты» / «спокойно»); below the cards the table «Где ликвидируют» (rows top-20, columns 1 h / 4 h / 24 h, cell = USD with background intensity by ratio in four steps and colour by dominant side, sorted by the 1 h ratio, row → /instrument/:symbol) and the feed «Крупные ликвидации» (threshold picker 50 k / 100 k / 500 k / 1 M, newest on top, polled 30 s). Honesty line everywhere (§12.4): «Binance: нет данных до запуска сервера» whenever venues.missing is non-empty. Plain Russian via the string tables (both languages), three-file components, pure mappers/formatters with specs. Done when: endpoint and mapper specs; a whole-app run on :3005 with the local Bybit+OKX tape; a screenshot of the landing page after /web login showing the card, the table and the feed. RATIO BASIS RULING 2026-10-12, after dev-3's IB-041 rehearsal: `coveredHours` has NO basis for the 2026-09-28..10-12 history, because collector_heartbeats arrived with migration 010 on 2026-10-12 and coverage is recorded forward only - it cannot be reconstructed backwards. dev-3 declined to seed heartbeats from the tape's first and last rows, which would have manufactured a satisfying '100 % covered' out of the very inference IB-BUG-010 exists to forbid (liveness derived from events). Therefore «× от нормы» must distinguish THREE states and never collapse them: coverage recorded -> divide by covered hours; coverage NOT recorded for the window -> refuse the ratio and say coverage is not recorded for this period, never falling back to elapsed hours; no events -> no norm. State (2) is the new one and it is the one that would otherwise silently become (1) or get divided by elapsed time, which is exactly the inflation this whole chain of tasks exists to prevent. The figure will acquire a real basis only from the next collector run on a migrated database.

title: The Bybit and OKX liquidation streams write no collector_gaps rows, so downtime is indistinguishable from a quiet market
description: Found by dev-2 while building IB-038's '× от нормы' figure. The Binance side is handled properly - degraded-gaps.ts writes binance-perp:forceOrder rows with repaired = 0, and there are 2 on the coordinator's tape - but the Bybit and OKX websocket liquidation collectors record nothing when they are not running. Consequence, measured on insight_coord: only 9 of the 226 hours since 2026-09-28 hold any liquidation at all (557 events across 2 venues), because the collectors were down through the pause, and nothing in the data says which hours were covered. Any statistic over that history - the 30-day median behind '× от нормы', a baseline, an anomaly score - silently treats downtime as a quiet market, drags the median down and inflates every later ratio. Fix: the ws liquidation collectors record their own uptime the way the degraded Binance path records its lost windows, so a consumer can divide by covered hours rather than elapsed hours; a gap row per spell with its reason, in the existing collector_gaps shape. Done when: a spec covers a collector stopping and restarting producing a row with the covered window; a statistic computed over a tape with a known outage uses covered hours and says so; and IB-038's ratio basis cites coverage rather than elapsed time. Widened 2026-10-12 (from the IB-BUG-011 review): the ingest side of the same blindness belongs here. A venue can write a symbol spelling that the `symbols` map has never heard of, and those rows are then unreachable from any canonical id - they sit in the table and reach no page, silently, exactly like the OKX rows did. dev-2 measured 0 unmapped on 2026-10-07, which is one day's measurement and not a guarantee. Add a count of liquidation rows whose (venue, symbol) matches no `symbols` spelling, surfaced on the coverage page beside the uptime rows, so the day it stops being 0 shows up as a number rather than as a quieter market.

title: The instrument page's liquidation query matches the raw symbol, so it shows one venue's rows while labelling them «все биржи»
description: Found by dev-2 reading the repo for IB-038; on master now, in the merged instrument view, and both IB-038 and IB-039 are about to build on it. apps/insight-bot/src/web/series/pg/series.repo.ts:161 filters `where symbol = $1`, but the liquidations table stores each venue's NATIVE symbol - bybit BTCUSDT vs okx BTC-USDT-SWAP, and 1000PEPEUSDT vs PEPE-USDT-SWAP for the same coin in different units. So a request for BTCUSDT with venue=all returns Bybit rows only, OKX can never match whatever venue is set to, and the response still says venue 'all' while the pane renders «все биржи». Measured on insight_dev2 for BTC over 24 h: bybit 9 events / 27,250 USD shown, okx 5 events / 236,565 USD silently dropped - the page shows about 10 % of the money and calls it all venues, reading as a quiet market. Fix: join through the symbols table (id with bybit_linear / okx_swap / binance_perp), which dev-2 verified maps every distinct symbol in liquidations today with 0 unmapped; plus a guard so an unmapped venue symbol is COUNTED and surfaced rather than dropped by the join, because the day a venue lists something symbols does not know about must appear as a number, not as a quieter market. Why no test caught it: the existing specs use fixture rows whose symbol already equals the queried one, so a missing join is invisible - the spec needs two venues' real symbol spellings in one table. Ruled to be fixed inside IB-038 as its own first commit, since that task needs the same join for «Где ликвидируют» and IB-039's markers depend on it being right.

title: The norm across a venue-set change: a dark ratio must carry a return date, and continuity must be labelled rather than substituted
description: Ruled 2026-10-12 on dev-2's IB-038 question. The «× от нормы» norm period is per scope, so when a venue joins the collected set the common period restarts and every ratio goes null for 7 days. That part is CORRECT and stays: a Binance-inclusive hour measured against a Bybit+OKX median overstates every window, which is a manufactured spike at the exact moment the data gets better, and §12.4 exists to prevent exactly that. What is missing is the two things that make the blackout a feature instead of a card that looks broken. (1) A dark figure must carry a RETURN DATE, derivable as min(ts) per venue plus seven days: «норма пересчитывается: binance в сборе с 20.10, множитель вернётся 27.10», not a bare «нет нормы». (2) Continuity must be OFFERED and LABELLED, never substituted: during a blackout the previous venue set's ratio is still honest if it names its set - «×2.3 к норме по bybit+okx; binance в расчёт не входит» - as a secondary line, never the headline, and never called «× от нормы» unqualified, because a multiple over a subset of the money with no label is IB-BUG-011 in a different hat. GATED: must be done BEFORE Binance liquidation collection starts, which sits behind IB-013 (the box), which the user deferred on 2026-10-12. So there is no race and it is not to be started now.

title: Consolidate the liquidation tapes: insight_dev2 holds the only copy of 2026-10-07 -> now, and the record has no gap after all
description: Measured 2026-10-12. insight_coord covers 2026-09-28 -> 2026-10-07 22:01:43 continuously (58 862 rows, no empty day) and stopped there on the user's order. insight_dev2, dev-2's slot, covers 2026-10-07 17:54:35 -> now and is STILL RUNNING. They overlap by about four hours and leave no gap, so the five days I reported to the user as lost forever - liquidations are websocket-only and no venue sells that history - are not lost: they exist in insight_dev2 and nowhere else. That also explains why dev-2's «× от нормы» refused on every window: the eight empty days were their slot's own history hole, not a quiet market, and on a consolidated tape a median exists and the figure fires. Job: copy the liquidation rows (and, while there, candles/OI/long-short/mark-funding for the same window) from insight_dev2 into insight_coord, de-duplicated on the natural key (venue, symbol, ts, side, price, qty) because the four-hour overlap WILL produce duplicates, verify the merged tape has no hour unaccounted for between 2026-09-28 and today, and report per-day counts before and after. Read-only on insight_dev2 - it is another slot's database and it is live; do not stop its collector and do not write to it. Until this is done, dev-2's slot collector is the only thing holding the recent tape, so nobody stops it. Related: IB-BUG-010 (nothing in either database distinguishes down from quiet, which is what made the hole look like a calm market). BACKUPS as of 2026-10-12 (dev-2): two pg_dump copies of the insight_dev2 tape - one job-scoped under ~/.claude/jobs/0028abca/tmp/reports/, one at ~/insight-tape-backups/ tied to neither job nor repo; both verified 32585/32585 rows, of which 27870 (2026-10-08..12) exist in no other database. dev-2 confirmed by `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` that the location is outside any repo, so `git clean` cannot reach it. CAVEAT, stated by dev-2 and not yet closed: the dumps are --data-only, so a restore needs the schema AND the monthly RANGE partitions to exist first - and there is deliberately no DEFAULT partition, so a restore into a fresh database fails loudly rather than silently mis-filing rows. Therefore: a dump whose restore has never been rehearsed is not yet insurance. Before this task is considered covered, rehearse the restore ONCE into a scratch database (test/db/scratch-db.ts has the helpers) - migrations, then partition maintenance, then the data-only load - and write the recipe, in order, next to the dump. That rehearsal is the cheapest possible version of IB-013's backup/restore drill and it proves the only copy of five days of websocket-only data can actually come back. RESTORE REHEARSED 2026-10-12 (dev-2) and it failed the first time, which is the point of rehearsing. Trap 1: `--table='liquidations*' --data-only` expands to 85 COPY statements naming each partition back to 2020, so with no DEFAULT partition the restore died on `relation liquidations_2020_01 does not exist`; the fix is `--load-via-partition-root`, which routes rows through the parent and lets partition maintenance place them. Trap 2, the dangerous one: the obvious correction `--table=liquidations` produced an EMPTY dump that `gzip -t` passed - a backup that is well-formed and holds nothing, which is the same family as IB-BUG-011's confident wrong number rather than a crash. Restored tape is now digest-identical to source at 32 594 rows; recipe and script live beside the dump at ~/insight-tape-backups/RESTORE.md. Consolidation into insight_coord is still to do; the data is no longer at risk while it waits. Result to expect: liquidations 58 863 -> 91 217 (32 354 inserted, 336 duplicates skipped), candles_1m -> 1 204 202, open_interest_5m -> 378 170, long_short_5m -> 1 512 466, mark_funding_1m -> 588 047, funding_settlements -> 155 087; 340 of the 345 hours from 09-28 10:00 to 10-12 18:00 hold liquidations, the five empty ones scattered singles plus one 2 h run (the shape of a quiet market, not an outage), and NO gap at the 10-07 -> 10-08 seam.
