title: The coverage page never completes on a populated database: monthsWithRows full-scans per symbol, 16.7 s each x ~120
description: Measured by dev-3 on 2026-10-12 while finishing IB-BUG-010, on a populated slot db (21.6 M candle rows): ONE pre-existing `monthsWithRows` call takes 16 735 ms for a single symbol, and the coverage controller runs about 120 of them (30 symbols x 4 series), so GET /api/web/coverage never completes - confirmed by the absence of any 'request completed' line for it in the server log while 52 other requests finished. PRE-EXISTING, in `backfill-reads.ts`, not introduced by IB-BUG-010; that task merely made it matter, because the new uptime block renders on the same page. For scale, dev-3's own new queries on the same page are 376 ms, 540 ms and 38 ms. Assigned to dev-2 because `backfill-reads.ts` is read by the backfill job and by dev-2's own code, and dev-3 flagged it instead of editing a file it does not own. REQUIREMENTS: (1) measure at least two shapes and report the numbers rather than assuming - dev-3's proposal is to generate the months between the extent and do one indexed `exists` probe per month (a full scan becomes ~81 index seeks), and the obvious alternative is one grouped pass for all symbols at once instead of 120 separate calls; say which won and by how much. (2) An equivalence spec: the new implementation must return exactly what the distinct-months scan returned, INCLUDING a symbol whose history has a hole in the middle, because 'generate the months between first and last' is wrong in precisely that case and an exists probe per month is what makes it right. (3) The backfill reads this too, so prove the backfill's use is unchanged, not only the web page's. Done when the coverage page renders against a populated database and the real screenshot replaces IB-BUG-010's scratch-database one.

title: The coverage page reports months as missing that hold data: date_trunc runs in the session zone while Node asks in UTC
description: Found by dev-2 during IB-042, pre-existing on master, deliberately NOT fixed inside IB-042 because that task's contract was to return exactly what the old scan returned and this changes what BOTH return. Two halves of one answer disagree about what a month is: `monthsWithRows` (backfill-reads.ts) truncates with `date_trunc('month', ts)` on a timestamptz, which truncates in the SESSION zone, while `missingBetween` (coverage.controller.ts) asks with `cursor.getUTCMonth()`, which is always UTC. This machine's session is US/Pacific, so a row at 2025-08-01T00:00Z is 2025-07-31 17:00 locally and lands in 2025-07; Node then asks whether 2025-08 is present, finds it is not, and reports a month that HOLDS DATA as missing. Demonstrated, not inferred: a fixture with rows at exactly 2025-08-01T00:00Z and 2025-09-30T23:59Z yields ['2025-07','2025-09'] from both implementations, and feeding that to the real missingBetween reports 2025-08 missing. Note the trap this exposes: IB-042's equivalence spec passes because the two implementations are wrong TOGETHER - an equivalence spec pins behaviour, it does not validate it, and that is worth remembering the next time one is used as evidence of correctness. Cost: every series whose first or last row falls inside the UTC offset of a month boundary gets a phantom missing month, on the page whose entire job is to say where history has holes - IB-BUG-011's class again, and worse here because it is wrong in the direction that INVENTS WORK: someone could re-backfill a month that was never missing. The reverse (a real hole hidden by the offset) follows from the same mechanism but dev-2 has not constructed it, so it is implied, not measured. FIX: both sides state UTC explicitly rather than inheriting a zone - the SQL truncates in UTC, Node keeps getUTCMonth, and a spec asserts the pair agrees with rows placed exactly ON a month boundary in UTC, which is the only fixture that can see this. Also trace the BACKFILL's use of monthsWithRows end to end: dev-2 found no evidence of harm there, because it compares against months it generates itself, but explicitly reported that as 'no evidence of harm' rather than 'proven safe' - close that properly. RAISED TO P0 2026-10-12 after dev-2 traced the backfill and CORRECTED THEIR OWN earlier 'no evidence of harm': the backfill IS harmed, and in the worse direction. monthsBetween builds UTC labels, monthsWithRows returns session-zone labels, and monthsToFetch filters one by the other - so storing exactly one UTC month (2025-08) makes monthsWithRows report {2025-07, 2025-08} and the backfill SKIPS July permanently, while the coverage page reports no gap because the same wrong label says July is present. THE TWO BUGS HIDE EACH OTHER: the detector and the fetcher share the mistake, so the hole is invisible to the only thing that looks for holes. TECH LEAD MEASUREMENT of how much damage already exists, so the fix does not ship with an unknown behind it: on insight_coord, comparing date_trunc('month', ts) against date_trunc('month', ts at time zone 'UTC'), the month-label SETS are IDENTICAL for every populated series - session-only labels none, UTC-only labels none, funding_settlements 80 months either way, earliest row 2020-03-25 09:00-07, well inside its month. So the defect is PROVEN IN MECHANISM AND LATENT IN THIS DATA: dense series put rows all through each month, so a mislabelled first-of-month row lands in a month that has its own rows anyway and the set does not change. It bites when a month's earliest row sits inside the UTC offset AND the previous month is otherwise empty - which is exactly a FRESH backfill against an EMPTY database, i.e. the Tokyo box's first boot. That is why it is P0 rather than merely correct-to-fix. REQUIRED beyond the fix: a one-time verification pass comparing the two labellings on every populated database, reporting the difference as a number so 'nothing was skipped' is measured rather than hoped; and after the fix, re-run the gap detection so anything previously skipped is fetched. VERIFIED 2026-10-12: dev-2's committed audit (`npm run audit:months`, read-only, exits non-zero on disagreement) found insight_coord clean as I had measured (0/0) but insight_dev2 NOT clean - 2 session-only labels, candles_1m/BTCUSDT -> 2019-12 and funding_settlements/BTCUSDT -> 2026-08, both caused by a first row sitting on a UTC month boundary, both outside the series extent so never user-visible. So the mechanism is realised in live data and my 'latent' measurement held only for the one database I checked. Gap-detection re-run over all 120 series: 0 missing before, 0 after, 0 changed, and the affected symbol now reports earliest 2020-01 instead of 2019-12, 82 months instead of 83 - one phantom month removed, nothing refetched.

title: The coverage page on the box: a 31.9 s cold request, and an uptime block that says «покрыто 0 из 0 часов»
description: Two things about the coverage page as a product, both raised 2026-10-12. (1) COLD PATH. After IB-042 the page is 1.15-1.3 s warm but 31.9 s on the first request after a restart, with Postgres's buffer cache cold. dev-2 reported the cold number instead of quoting only the warm one and said plainly that nothing in IB-042 fixes it. On the box this is the path that will hurt: a t4g.small has 1 GB of RAM and therefore a much smaller cache. RULING: a per-request cache (IB-038's shape) is NOT the fix, because it does nothing for the first visitor, who is the one who complains; prefer a periodically refreshed summary so the page reads something already computed. And MEASURE IT ON THE BOX rather than here - the cache size is the whole variable, so a figure from a 64 GB laptop says nothing about a 1 GB instance. Gated behind IB-013. (2) THE BASIS LINE. On a slot whose collector predates IB-BUG-010 the uptime block renders «покрыто 0 из 0 часов работы сборщиков». That is the same defect IB-BUG-010 correctly avoided per stream - a stream with no heartbeat is omitted rather than drawn at 0 % - reappearing at the aggregate: 0 of 0 asserts a measurement where none exists. It must say that coverage is not recorded for this window, matching the three-state ruling on IB-038 (recorded / not recorded / no events). This half is small and not gated; do it first. Part (1) MERGED at e71418f 2026-10-12 (the basis line now says coverage is not recorded rather than «0 из 0»); part (2), the 31.9 s cold request, remains open and gated behind IB-013 with the measurement to be taken ON the box. Ruling recorded with it: the coverage block carries TWO states permanently - were we listening or not - and never event counts; «nothing was liquidated» is a statement about the tape and lives in IB-038's ratio, because two subjects on one surface is how a detector and a consumer came to share a wrong assumption in IB-043.

title: What history does each feature key actually need, and which of it can ever be obtained? A dated map before the frame goes live
description: Raised by the Tech Lead 2026-10-12 after measuring insight_coord against IB-015's requirements, because the feature engine is about to be correct and empty. MEASURED DEPTH TODAY: candles_1m 9 days (2026-09-28..10-07, 31 symbols), candles_agg 10 days, open_interest_5m 39 days (from 2026-08-29), long_short_5m 39 days, funding_settlements 6.5 years (2020-03-25, 59 symbols). IB-015's groups need: funding percentiles over 90 settlements (SATISFIED - about 30 days at 8 h, and we hold years), but Wilder ATR(14) percentiles over 90 days, OI percentiles over 90 days and long/short percentiles over 90 days are ALL short. So most percentile keys would refuse, correctly, and the frame would publish little; worse, IB-016's regime axes (vol band = ATR 4h percentile over 90 days; leverage = OI percentile over 90 days) and the playbooks behind them inherit that emptiness. THE JOB IS A DATED MAP, not a backfill run: for every key in the registry, state the history it requires, what is held now, what can be FETCHED (Binance archive at data.binance.vision is bulk files and nearly free in weight; klines go back years), and what can only ACCRUE FORWARD because the venue does not serve it. The last category is the one that matters: OI and long/short history is widely believed to have a short REST retention window, and BUG-022 records that this repo once wrote that retention backwards from a single probe, so MEASURE it per venue under AGENTS.md's repetition rule (at least 5 observations per boundary on two occasions minutes apart) rather than quoting a number. Deliverable: a table of key -> required history -> available now -> obtainable by backfill -> earliest date the key can first be computed, with the Binance REST weight per minute of anything that polls, and a plain-Russian paragraph for the user saying which parts of the product are gated on time passing rather than on work. If a backfill closes a gap, say its size and cost; do not run a multi-day fetch without bringing the number to me first. OUTCOME 2026-10-12: THE PREMISE OF THIS TASK WAS WRONG AND THE MAP DISPROVED IT. 20 of 22 key groups are computable TODAY. I had read the '90 days' from design 8.2 prose (and from my own wording of this task) instead of from the COMMITTED REGISTRY, which is the authoritative artefact and which dev-2 had deliberately hoisted the constants into so the requirement is readable in one place. What the registry actually asks for: oi percentile days:7; long/short percentile days:30 minPeriods:45; wilder atr period:14 BARS at 1h/4h/1d; liquidation z-score windowMinutes:60 lookbackDays:30 minHistoryDays:14; and the only 90 in the whole contract is funding settlements:90, which at 8 h is 30 days against the 2387 days of funding history we hold. Held today: OI and long/short 36.5-39 days, so both satisfied. Only two keys are short: atr.1d.14, which needs 14 daily bars and resolves by itself within days, and liq.*.z60m, which IB-041's tape consolidation unlocks outright - so the user's one consolidation command has moved from housekeeping to unblocking a feature key. MEASURED VENUE FACT, to AGENTS.md's repetition rule: Binance OI/long-short REST retention is 30 days EXACTLY, and past it the venue REFUSES rather than returning an empty series - two rounds of observations, which matters because a refusal is detectable while an empty response would read as 'no data'. No fetch was started. Map committed at architecture/insight-bot-history-map.md.

title: «× от нормы» divides by a dust median: $500k against a $0.18 norm renders as «×2 700 000»
description: Found by dev-2 2026-10-12 during the float-guard sweep the Tech Lead ordered after the sd === 0 residue bug. NOT the same bug, and dev-2 checked rather than assumed: a median of exact zeros is exactly zero, so IB-038's `median === 0` guard holds for the case it was written for. But it is exposed to a legitimately TINY median by a different route - measured on insight_dev2, the smallest non-zero hourly liquidation sum is $0.1848 and the first percentile of non-zero hours is $5.44, so a $500k hour against a $0.18 norm renders as «×2 700 000 от нормы» on a user-facing card. NOT currently reachable, also measured: every coin's hourly median on today's tape is exactly 0, so the existing guard catches all of them. Fixed anyway because it is one comparison on a card the user reads: a median below WEB_LIQUIDATION_MIN_NORM_USD ($1) is dust rather than a norm and the ratio refuses, while the median itself is still reported so the card can say what it saw. The $1 is a JUDGEMENT stated as one - above the $0.18 floor, well below the $5.44 first percentile - not dressed up as a measurement. Fixed inside the ib-feature-frame branch as its own commit because it was found there, in the same shape as IB-BUG-011 riding inside IB-038: own id, own commit, reviewable separately from the feature work. REQUIRED with it: a spec that pins the judgement to its reasoning rather than to the number - a median of $0.18 refuses, a median of $5.44 produces a ratio - so a later tuning of the constant has to confront what it was for.

title: Input completeness is evaluated per GROUP against its widest window, so keys that need one bar refuse whenever a 24 h key in the same group is short
description: Found by dev-1 2026-10-12 while producing IB-018's arming audit, and verified by the Tech Lead in the source. gather.ts computes the lookback PER INPUT GROUP (`const from = until - lookbackMs(group)`, and the shortfall type is documented as 'one per input group'), so a group's window is the widest any key in it needs. `px.close`, `px.high` and `px.low` declare `window: 'frame bar'` - one bar - while `px.ret_24h` and `px.drawdown_from_24h_high` declare `params: { hours: 24 }`, and all five name `agg:15m`. Consequence, measured: across 477 backfilled frames the px.* keys refused 477/477 with incomplete_input, while 422 of those closes HAD their own 15m bar complete. The refusal fails safe, and that is exactly what makes it dangerous - an over-refusal is indistinguishable from an honest one, so the system reports itself as more data-starved than it is and nobody can tell. It is the inverse of the day's other defects: not a confident wrong number but a confident 'cannot know' when we could. SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE, which is the reason this is P1 rather than P2: several decisions today were argued from 'these keys refuse', including IB-045's history map and IB-016's axes table, so those figures must be RE-MEASURED after the fix - and more seriously, an over-refusal is precisely the pressure that would make someone loosen armKeys or lower minPeriods, which is the one thing IB-018 was dispatched forbidding. FIX: evaluate completeness per KEY against that key's own window. The registry already carries it - `window` plus `params.hours` / `params.period` / `params.settlements` - so the data exists and no contract change is needed. Keep the group read (one query per group, widest window) for efficiency, but attribute the shortfall per key. BLAST RADIUS BOUNDED 2026-10-12 by dev-1, correcting the Tech Lead's over-broad claim in the paragraph above: IB-016's axes table and P3's ~2026-10-26 arming date are NOT affected and do NOT need re-measuring. The axes table was sourced from REGIME_SPEC, the frame registry and the RAW tables, none of which pass through gather.ts's group completeness; the arming date derives from when collector_heartbeats begin plus the 14-day minimum history, i.e. from `not_recorded` and `explained_absence`, and the defect manufactures neither of those - it manufactures only `incomplete_input`. IB-045's history map is likewise raw-table depth and unaffected. So the ONLY figures that move are the incomplete_input lines in IB-018's arming audit, which dev-1 will re-run with per-key deltas once this lands. Recorded because an over-broad invalidation is its own cost: re-measuring things that were never wrong consumes exactly the attention the real fix needs, and my 'those figures must be re-measured' was the eleventh over-scoped claim I made today.

title: sameValue compares jsonb via JSON.stringify, so key reordering reports ~17k false value conflicts a day
description: Found by dev-1 2026-10-12 re-running IB-018's arming audit after IB-047. `sameValue` serialises with JSON.stringify and compares strings; Postgres jsonb does not preserve key order, so a stored {count, of} comes back reordered and compares unequal to the freshly computed object even when nothing changed. Measured: 954 false conflicts in one audit window, extrapolating to about 17 000 a day in production. TWO guarantees break at once, which is why this is P1. (a) IDEMPOTENCY: the rule is that a re-check producing identical values writes NOTHING, and a false conflict writes a revision - so append-only quietly becomes grows-forever, the exact failure dev-2 spec'd against with a five-iteration loop, which could not see it because its fixture values round-trip through JSON.stringify identically. (b) THE DATA-DEFECT SIGNAL: a changed published value is ruled to be a data defect surfaced as a number, never a silent update - and 17 000 false defects a day buries every real one. An alarm that fires 17k times for harmless reasons is an alarm nobody reads, which is the same failure mode as a no-gaps migration rule. FIX: compare semantically rather than by serialisation - a deep equality that is insensitive to object key order, or a canonical key ordering applied on both sides before comparison. Whichever is chosen, the spec must use a fixture whose keys are stored in one order and computed in another, because a fixture that round-trips identically cannot see this.

title: A new registry key can never reach a published frame, so historical closes are permanently unevaluable for any playbook needing it
description: Found by dev-1 2026-10-12: `decideAmendment` can turn a refusal into a value but can never ADD a key that was absent from a published frame, so px.high and px.low are permanently absent on all 477 older closes on insight_dev1 and P3 can never arm there. RULED: this is CORRECT behaviour, not a defect in decideAmendment. A frame is immutable in its key SET - amendment fills refusals within a version, and a different key set is a different version. Retroactively adding keys would make a frame claim to be a version-N frame containing version-N+1 keys, which is precisely what frame_version exists to prevent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the consequence: the version-freeze condition was crossed TODAY. When the three IB-016 keys and then px.high/px.low were added, `feature_frames` held 0 rows and `feature_frame_versions` was empty, which is why keeping WEB_FRAME_VERSION at 1 was free and correct. 477 frames now exist. So (1) the NEXT key addition must bump the version; (2) historical closes acquire new keys only by BACKFILLING at the new version, never by amendment, with both versions' frames retained and read version-aware per the 2026-10-12 ruling; (3) dev-2 must say what assertFrameVersionFingerprint does right now on a slot holding version-1 frames written under an older key set than the live registry - it was built to throw on exactly that mismatch, and if it does not fire here, the mechanism that was supposed to make this impossible is itself not working. ANSWERED 2026-10-12 by dev-2, and the answer is the bigger finding: the guard never fires because THE CLAIM ROW WAS NEVER WRITTEN. `features.cli --symbol` calls runClose, which bypasses the claim entirely. Tech Lead measurement across slots: insight_dev1 holds 905 frames and 0 claim rows; insight_dev2 holds 99 frames and 1 claim row - so the claiming path works and the backfill CLI, which writes in bulk, skips it. THE HAZARD IS WORSE THAN NO GUARD: the first write through the claiming path would insert the CURRENT fingerprint and retroactively legitimise 905 frames computed under a different key set, so the mechanism would end up asserting something false. RULINGS: (1) close the bypass STRUCTURALLY, not by adding a call - the claim belongs inside the write primitive so a caller cannot skip it, because 'remember to claim' is a rule and today has eight examples of rules losing to mechanisms; (2) the 905 unclaimed frames are DISCARDED and re-backfilled under a claimed version, never retroactively claimed - they are derived data, reproducible from the raw tables by the history mode, and claiming them would be the one action that makes the guard lie; (3) recorded against BOTH of us: we each read 'feature_frame_versions is empty' as 'no frames are persisted, so the version is still free', when it actually meant 'the claim path was never used'. An empty table was taken as evidence about WRITES when it was evidence about CLAIMS, and I used that reading twice to argue the version could stay at 1. MEASURED BY THE TECH LEAD 2026-10-12, which both narrows and widens this. `feature_frames` has NO fingerprint column - the columns are symbol, tf, close_time, frame_version, keys, basis, complete, incomplete_reason, computed_at, computed_mode, revision, amended_at, amended_keys - so a frame records the WEAK identifier (a human-assigned version we deliberately did not bump) and not the STRONG one (the fingerprint that actually identifies the key set). The mixture is nevertheless recoverable by inspecting the stored key set: on insight_dev1, 903 frames carry 45 keys (the 7a4a2a87 set) and 2 carry 47 (14f15ddd), with the boundary today. ADDED REQUIREMENT, and it is the better fix: EACH FRAME RECORDS THE SPEC FINGERPRINT IT WAS COMPUTED UNDER. Then a version-versus-key-set mismatch is detectable per row, a retroactive claim cannot be made silently, and the claim table becomes a cross-check rather than the sole record. This is the same move as venuesPresent, the ratio basis, computed_mode and frame_revision - a derived row carries what it was derived from - and had it been there, this whole episode would have diagnosed itself. URGENT ORDERING: no guarded pass may run on insight_dev1 before the 905 frames are dropped, because the claim is `on conflict do nothing` with the LIVE fingerprint, so the first guarded write would certify 14f15ddd as version 1 and the 903 frames at 45 keys would become indistinguishable from the 2 at 47.

title: context.service.spec reads the wall clock, so the suite is red for ten minutes every day and its sibling is vacuous for the other 23h50m
description: Found by dev-2 2026-10-12/13 and verified by the Tech Lead at 2026-10-13T00:04:14Z. apps/insight-bot/test/collectors/context/context.service.spec.ts calls `tick(new Date())`, and schedule.ts documents the per-coin daily cap as due at 00:10 UTC - so between 00:00 and 00:10 UTC the daily pass is not yet due and the test fails, while for the remaining 23 h 50 m its NEIGHBOUR passes vacuously, because the pass being due is what it needed to assert anything. THE PAIR THEREFORE PROVIDES NO COVERAGE AT ANY TIME: one is red exactly when the other is meaningful. Present since IB-036 and unnoticed because nobody had run the suite inside the window until tonight. CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING: every green run reported on 2026-10-12 - 1481 tests and the rest - was green partly because of WHEN it ran, which makes each of those reports a weaker statement than it appeared. FIX: inject the clock, the way dev-2 threaded it through the news poller earlier the same day after finding tick(now) injected while pollOne read Date.now(); then assert BOTH sides, a close before 00:10 and one after, so neither case can be vacuous. The precedent and the pattern already exist in this repo.

title: Partially-threaded clocks: 12 modules accept an injected now AND call Date.now() directly — classify them, then make the mixture fail
description: Two CONFIRMED instances were found independently on 2026-10-12/13 in different code by different people: dev-2's news poller (tick(now) injected while pollOne stamped Date.now()) and dev-1's context service (tick(now) took an instant while primeThenBackfill, pollGlobalGuarded and the stamps read Date.now(), which marked lastDailyDay 10-13 while the spec asked 10-12 and made a duplicate-suppression spec read six fetches where it expected three). Two independent instances in one day make it a pattern in this codebase rather than two incidents. TECH LEAD SWEEP, and these are SUSPECTS not defects - a module can legitimately take a `now` for domain time while using Date.now() for elapsed wall time such as a timeout, and classifying them is the first job, not fixing them: calendar-collector.service.ts (4 direct calls), context.service.ts (4), oi-ls.poller.ts (4), okx.service.ts (2), features.runner.ts (2), derive.runner.ts (2), mark-sampler.ts (1), recheck-schedule.ts (1), overview.service.ts (1), reaction.service.ts (1), news.service.ts (1), gap-report.service.ts (1). WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: a partially threaded clock makes tests pass while production runs two clocks that disagree, and it is undetectable from either side - the test sees the injected instant, the code sees the real one, and nothing compares them. It also produces the worst kind of test: IB-050's pair gave no coverage at any time because one side was red exactly when the other was meaningful. THEN THE MECHANISM, per the refuse-not-warn rule: a spec that FAILS when a module taking an injected clock also calls Date.now(), with an explicit allow-list whose every entry carries its reason - the same shape as dev-1's import-boundary guard and dev-3's migration-version spec. A rule saying 'thread the clock properly' is the kind that lost three times today.

title: Recursive indicators are fed the group window, so ATR and EMA values depend on coverage rather than on the market
description: Found by dev-2 on 2026-10-13 while investigating the 84 genuine atr.1h.14 conflicts dev-1's derive run surfaced, after the Tech Lead's hypothesis (that candles_agg.complete could be true for a partially-derived bucket) was REFUTED by measurement: 0 of 152 944 complete buckets across both slots have a wrong bar count, so the completeness flag is trustworthy. REAL CAUSE: wilderAtr is fed the GROUP window rather than its own declared bars, and Wilder smoothing is RECURSIVE - ATR(14) over 24 bars is not ATR(14) over 100 bars, because the recursion converges but never exactly. So the published value is a function of HOW MUCH HISTORY HAPPENED TO BE AVAILABLE, not of the market, and a derive run that adds bars changes it. Measured consequence: 84 conflicts on atr.1h.14, mean 13.30, max 52.55. The same defect hits the EMAs for the same reason. AFFECTED KEYS: atr.1h.14, atr.4h.14, atr.1d.14, ema.4h.50, ema.1d.200 - and everything reading them, which is IB-016's vol band (ATR percentile) and trend axis (both EMAs), and P3's stop, trigger and T1, all of which are ATR multiples. FIX: feed each recursive indicator a FIXED declared window - period (or length) plus a stated warm-up - so the value is reproducible regardless of what else is available, with the warm-up in the registry params so it is inside the fingerprint. THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and the positive control for this whole class: feed the calculator MORE history than its window and assert the value is IDENTICAL. A recursive indicator that is not invariant to extra history is reading coverage. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE VERSION: adding a warm-up param changes the fingerprint, and frames now exist (961 on insight_dev1, 5 on insight_dev2), so this is the FIRST change that must bump WEB_FRAME_VERSION - the condition set up in IB-049, arriving three hours later.

title: frame_version is not in the frames key and the conflicts table is version-blind, so 'keep v1, read version-aware' is not implementable and a definition change reads as a data defect
description: Found by dev-1 on 2026-10-13 by trying ONE close before running a v2 pass over existing v1 frames - which is why this is a discovery rather than a database full of false conflicts. Verified by the Tech Lead: feature_frames_pkey is PRIMARY KEY (symbol, tf, close_time, revision) with NO frame_version, so a v2 frame for an existing close cannot be written at all; and feature_value_conflicts holds (symbol, tf, close_time, revision, feature_key, published, recomputed, seen_at) with NO frame_version, so a conflict row cannot even record which definition each side came from. CONSEQUENCE OBSERVED: the pass compared v2 recomputations against v1 published values and recorded the DEFINITION CHANGE as data defects - atr.4h.14 going 'value -> insufficient_history' into feature_value_conflicts, which reads as an input vanishing when it is only v2 needing 71 four-hourly bars. THE TECH LEAD'S RULING OF 2026-10-12 - keep v1 frames and read them version-aware, never recompute in place - was correct in intent and UNIMPLEMENTABLE as stated, because it assumed a key that does not exist. Third time that day a ruling needed a storage change that had not been verified. FIX, migration 017, dev-2's since they own the schema and the version machinery: (1) frame_version joins the frames key, (symbol, tf, close_time, frame_version, revision), so v1 and v2 coexist and amendments stay inside a version; (2) feature_value_conflicts gains frame_version and conflicts are computed WITHIN a version only - v2 against v2, never v2 against v1 - because across versions the definition changed and a difference is expected rather than defective; (3) a cross-version comparison is genuinely useful but is a SEPARATE labelled artefact, never a conflict row - it is 'what the definition change did to the numbers', which is the thirty-symbol measurement dev-2 already made for IB-052, generalised. LEDGER CORRECTED 2026-10-13: I double-promised 017 - reserved for IB-016's regime storage, then given to IB-053 - by allocating from memory after saying the ledger was a record and not an allocator. dev-1 caught it. NO NUMBER IS RESERVED FOR ANYONE. Under the merge-time rule the number is taken immediately before the fast-forward and must equal master_highest + 1, enforced by the uniqueness and burned-gap guards; a reservation is the thing that rule abolished, and holding one in my head is how 012-015 got burned in the first place. The ledger records USED and BURNED only: used 001-012 and 015-016; burned 013 and 014. Whoever merges next takes 017, whoever merges after that takes 018.

title: The twin-arm frame pin becomes its own table, so two arms or two revisions cannot disagree
description: Merged d6f6934 2026-10-13 behind IB-053. The pin was a frame_revision COLUMN on playbook_evaluations - a per-arm, per-revision row - so nothing could force two arms to carry the same revision and a new revision could silently carry a different one; the 'spans arms' property was enforced by logic rather than by a key, and adding revisions to that ledger would have broken it invisibly. Now playbook_frame_pins, PRIMARY KEY (playbook, symbol, close_time, source_mode) - verified on insight_dev2 - with NO arm column, whose absence is the entire content of the table. pinFrame claims and reads in ONE statement, so the only way to learn the pin is to offer one: an arm cannot proceed on an unclaimed assumption and cannot lose a read-then-write race. Settled by CONTENT - the lowest revision wins - so a race is resolved deterministically rather than by arrival order. Done while playbook_evaluations held 0 rows, which made it a schema change with no data migration; that window would have closed at the first evaluation write.

title: Backfill 1d candles from the venue archive: ema.1d.200 needs 600 daily bars and no derive can ever produce them
description: Measured 2026-10-13. ema.1d.200 requires length 200 + warmupBars 400 = 600 daily bars (IB-052). dev-1 measured the tape at 72 days of span, and the Tech Lead measured the actual complete 1d bars at 1001 across 31 symbols - about 32 per symbol - because a 1d aggregate can only be derived for a day with full underlying coverage. So the shortfall is NOT derive lag and no derive run can fix it: the days were never collected, and they have to be fetched. IB-045's history map established that Binance archive klines go back years and are bulk files, nearly free in request weight, so the data is available. NOT ON THE 2026-10-26 PATH, and this must not be confused with it: P3's armKeys are liq.*.z60m, oi.d4h_pct, funding.predicted.binance, px.drawdown_from_24h_high, atr.1h.14 and the three px bar keys - none of them is an EMA. The 26 October date is liquidation-coverage-bound and unaffected by this task. What this blocks is IB-016's TREND axis, and therefore any playbook whose context gate reads regime.trend. Done when: 600 complete daily bars exist per signal-set symbol, the trend axis stops refusing with insufficient_history on current closes, and the fetch's request weight per minute is stated in the report as for any venue poller. Note dev-1's cleared second blocker for contrast: atr.1h.14 went 188 refusals to 0 because 846 of 888 missing 1h bars WERE derivable from a 99.6 percent complete 1m tape - the opposite case, and the reason this one needed measuring rather than assuming. THREE FIGURES IN THIS BRIEF WERE WRONG, all mine, all corrected by dev-1 on 2026-10-13 and all shrinking the task. (1) I divided 1001 complete 1d bars by 31 SYMBOLS to get ~32 each; the rows are keyed by symbol AND market, so it is 60 series and 16.7 each. That is the spot+perp conflation for the THIRD time in one day - dev-1's flip rate, my 6841-bar query, and now this - and twice it was mine. (2) The average hides the symbol that matters: BTCUSDT perp holds 71 daily bars, four times the mean, because its 1m tape is 73 days where most symbols have 14. A mean across a heterogeneous population is the wrong statistic when one member is the one being tested, and BTC is the symbol every audit and P3 itself uses. (3) 'No derive can ever produce them' is wrong: a derive DOES produce 1d bars wherever the 1m tape supports them - dev-1 moved BTC perp 36 -> 71 in 48 seconds. The correct statement is that derive produces what the 1m tape covers and the archive supplies only the remainder. REQUIRED SEQUENCING, from dev-1: DERIVE FIRST, THEN SIZE THE ARCHIVE FETCH. Deriving what we already hold both reduces the fetch and reveals the true gap - 529 archive days for BTC perp rather than 564. Do not fetch before deriving; the number you would be sizing against is not the real one.

title: Tape-versus-aggregate coverage: report which candles_agg gaps are DERIVABLE and which need a venue backfill
description: Offered by dev-1 2026-10-13 and accepted. Compare candles_1m against candles_agg per symbol, market and tf, and report the gaps split by CAUSE - the distinction that cost hours three separate times tonight and was resolved by an ad-hoc query each time: (a) a gap in the aggregate with the 1m bars PRESENT is DERIVABLE, and the action is to run derive; (b) a gap with the 1m bars ABSENT is not derivable and needs a venue backfill. Those two present IDENTICALLY in every refusal count - insufficient_history or incomplete_input either way - and only a query against the layer below separates them. WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE: it would have surfaced the 480 px.drawdown_from_24h_high refusals, the 188 atr.1h.14 refusals and the 1d shortfall WEEKS before a playbook audit stumbled on each of them, and all three were found by accident through different routes. TWO REQUIREMENTS. (1) It REPORTS, it does not act: a check that triggers a derive hides the very gap it exists to surface, and the decision to derive over a window is a judgement about cost and timing. (2) It surfaces WHERE SOMEONE ALREADY LOOKS - the coverage page, beside dev-3's uptime and field-presence blocks - not only as a CLI, because an honesty figure whose only consumer is a command nobody runs is latent. A CLI is the right engine; the page is the required consumer. Also key it by symbol AND market: the spot/perp conflation was the single most repeated measurement error of 2026-10-12/13, three instances, twice by the Tech Lead.

title: The derive job only writes forward, so a 1m backfill leaves every aggregate layer empty behind it — the single root cause of three separate 'insufficient history' findings
description: Unified 2026-10-13 from two independent discoveries that turned out to be one defect. dev-1: 63 718 DERIVABLE 15m buckets across 60 series - verified by the Tech Lead, 58 of 60 series have no 15m aggregate before 2026-09-28 while the 1m tape reaches back to 2026-07-31 for all 60, and the only two series with history are the BTCUSDT pair dev-1 derived by hand that night, so the exception proves the rule. dev-2: BTC 1d went 13 -> 599 and 4h 99 -> 3597 in 107 seconds of derive, and ema.4h.50 needed NO archive fetch at all. ROOT CAUSE: the derive job (IB-014) writes forward from whenever it started, the archive backfill (IB-012) fetches 1m, and NOTHING derives the aggregates over the history the fetch brought in. So every 'insufficient_history' refusal investigated on 2026-10-12/13 - 480 drawdown, 188 atr.1h.14, the 1d shortfall I wrongly called unfetchable - was the same hole seen through three different keys. CONSEQUENCE IF NOT FIXED: the box reproduces it on first boot, and every symbol added to the universe reproduces it again, each time presenting as a data problem rather than as a pass nobody ran. FIX: the backfill path must derive the aggregates over the range it fetched, or state loudly that it has not; and a symbol newly added to the universe must get the same treatment. IB-056 is the detector for this and stays - a report is still wanted after the pipeline is fixed, because a fixed pipeline with a silent failure is indistinguishable from a broken one. SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-10-13 — the Tech Lead's supporting measurement was wrong and dev-1 caught it. I ran `select min(open_time), count(distinct symbol||market) from candles_1m` and read `2026-07-31 | 60` as 'the 1m tape reaches 07-31 for all 60 series'. It is a GLOBAL minimum beside a GLOBAL count: two independent aggregates in one row, read as a joint property. The per-series query - which I had written correctly twice earlier the same night and then did not use here - says: 4 series reach 2026-07-31 with ~103 982 rows each (BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT, spot and perp), and 56 start 2026-09-28 with ~20 460 rows, i.e. 14 days. SO FOR 56 OF 60 SERIES THE 15m HISTORY IS NOT DERIVABLE: the 1m is not there to derive from. dev-1's 63 718 figure is real but CONCENTRATED - ETH 6358 x2 plus BTC 3382 x2 = 19 480 from the four deep series, and 790 each from the 56 shallow ones, which is only their own 14-day window and IS genuine derive lag. CORRECTED ORDER: (1) derive what is derivable now, about 44 000 buckets across the 56 plus the 19 480 on the deep four; (2) fetch 1m for the SIGNAL SET only, as already authorised, 3 symbols; (3) derive again over what the fetch brought. The deep history of the other 56 series is NOT on any current path - frames are BTCUSDT-only, the signal set is three symbols - so it must not be fetched on the strength of the 63 718 figure. The root cause in the paragraph above is unchanged and still the unifying defect; only the scope was mine to get wrong.

Решение пользователя: опрос бота (не WS Binance из браузера); свечи (и taker delta/CVD из них) каждые 5 с, остальные панели (OI, фандинг, long/short, ликвидации, топ-50, сводка) раз в минуту. Сделать: чистая appendLater(current, tail) в pane-merge.ts (бар с тем же time заменяется, новые дописываются; флаг extendsLater) со spec; планировщик в новом live-tail.ts (не в компоненте): отброс по generation, один запрос в полёте на вид данных, пауза на скрытой вкладке и догон при возврате (разрыв больше окна — полный load()), остановка в DestroyRef, такт пропускается во время loading/loadingEarlier; график сохраняет вид, а у правого края следует за новой свечой — логика вида чистым файлом со spec, instrument-chart.component.ts не растёт. Бот: хвост в CandlesService (IB-063) идёт на биржу малым limit, а не страницей кэша; незакрытая свеча не кэшируется; вес в комментарии (~12/мин на вкладку при limit<100 = вес 1 по документации Binance); Cache-Control: no-store на хвосте. Конфликты: трогает те же файлы, что календарь (IB-060/061: instrument-window, pane-data, pane-merge, panel-series), IB-063 (CandlesService) и IB-065 (time-range, time-grid, выравнивание 1w) — начинать только когда все три в master. Готово: specs (appendLater, планировщик на fake timers, вид у правого края), npm test в apps/chart-client и jest бота зелёные; вживую: на 1m последняя свеча меняется ≤5 с и новая появляется на границе минуты без смены ТФ, прокрутка назад не прыгает, скрытая вкладка не шлёт запросов, вес в /health растёт ≤12/мин на вкладку. План: ~/.claude/plans/encapsulated-bouncing-giraffe.md.

title: Предстоящие события календаря на графике справа от текущей свечи
description: Пользователь 2026-10-29: предстоящие события календаря должны быть видны прямо на графике, справа от текущей свечи. Отдельная доработка к IB-060. Сейчас не видны по двум причинам: (1) instrument-window.ts читает calendarEvents(fromMs, toMs) с toMs = now — будущих событий в ответе нет; (2) calendar-marks.ts / time-marks.primitive.ts привязывают метку к candleTimes, а lightweight-charts не даёт координату времени правее последнего бара без whitespace-данных. Сделать: читать календарь до now + горизонт; добавить в ценовую серию whitespace-бары ({time}) в будущее с шагом ТФ (выравнивание 1w по понедельнику — как в IB-065), горизонт = до последнего известного события в пределах 7 дней, но не больше 200 баров ТФ (1m ≈ 3 ч 20 мин, 15m ≈ 50 ч, 1h ≈ 8 сут) — числа в чистой функции со spec; линии будущих событий рисуются так же, как прошедшие, с подсказкой и отметкой «через N ч/мин»; полосы выходных/праздников США тоже продолжаются вправо. Связка с IB-066: живой хвост заменяет whitespace-бар настоящей свечой по time (appendLater), следование за правым краем считает краем последнюю НАСТОЯЩУЮ свечу, а не whitespace; полоса времени (time-axis-strip, IB-064) показывает время и над будущими барами. Лента ForexFactory отдаёт только текущую неделю: события следующей недели появятся в понедельник — так и написать в подсказке/легенде не нужно, но указать в отчёте. Компоненты: instrument-chart.component.ts не растёт (сейчас 244), логика — чистыми файлами со spec. Готово: npm test в apps/chart-client зелёный; вживую на 15m и 1h справа от текущей свечи видны линии предстоящих событий недели с подсказкой, выходные затенены вперёд, живое обновление (IB-066) не ломает вид и заменяет пустые бары настоящими.

title: Пузыри ликвидаций сводятся по барам на сервере — без отказа при >2000 событий
description: Пользователь 2026-10-29: пузыри ликвидаций пропадают на 3m, 5m, 1W (и 4h/1d), потому что /api/web/series/liquidations/events отказывает 400 RANGE_TOO_WIDE при >2000 событий (WEB_MAX_LIQUIDATION_EVENTS), а клиент тогда рисует ноль пузырей. Решение пользователя: суммировать на сервере. Клиент и так сводит события в один пузырь на бар (liquidation-markers.adapter.ts: сумма USD, VWAP цены, число событий, сторона с большей суммой). Перенести это сведение на сервер: необязательный параметр tf (WebTimeframe) у /liquidations/events → SQL group by (начало бара через floorToGrid из range.ts — 1w с понедельника, side, venue): sum(usd), VWAP цены (sum(price*usd)/sum(usd)), count, max(usd). Контракт — аддитивно: WebLiquidationEventSchema получает необязательные count и maxUsd; форма события не меняется, чтобы живой хвост IB-066 (appendLater по liquidationEvents) и pane-merge работали без правок. С tf лимит 2000 не применяется (число строк ограничено бары×2 стороны×биржи — проверить и записать верхнюю границу в комментарии; если всё равно больше — отказ с понятным сообщением, а не обрезка). Без tf — как сейчас (другие потребители). Клиент: insight-api.client.ts передаёт tf; адаптер пузырей суммирует count вместо +1 и показывает в подсказке число ликвидаций и самую крупную. venuesPresent и undercounted — как сейчас. Не трогать pane-merge.ts, panel-series.ts, instrument-chart.component.ts, instrument.component.ts, time-range.ts — там работает dev-3 (IB-066/067); если без правки instrument-window.ts не обойтись — одна строка (передать timeframe) и сказать в отчёте. Готово: spec SQL-агрегации на insight_dev2 (бакет 1w по понедельнику, VWAP, count, разделение по side/venue), spec адаптера с count, jest бота и npm test зелёные; вживую на дашборде слота пузыри есть на 3m, 5m, 1h, 4h, 1d, 1W, и ни одного 400 от liquidations/events.

title: Push-уведомления в браузер через service worker: предстоящие события календаря
description: Пользователь 2026-10-29: push-уведомления в браузер через service worker — приходят и при закрытой вкладке дашборда (пока запущен браузер). Пока только о предстоящих событиях календаря. Сейчас (IB-061) уведомление в браузере есть только при открытой вкладке: calendar-alerts.service.ts + alerts-toggle.component.ts, дедуп в localStorage. Сервер уже решает «что и когда» для Telegram (IB-062): delivery/calendar-notifier.service.ts, calendar-notify.ts, журнал calendar_notifications_sent. Сделать: Web Push по стандарту (VAPID). Бот: библиотека web-push, ключи VAPID в env.schema (WEB_PUSH_VAPID_PUBLIC/PRIVATE/SUBJECT; без них канал выключен с понятной строкой в логе, бот грузится), новая таблица push-подписок (миграция — номер взять следующий свободный, проверить ВСЕ ref'ы и что WD-006 не занял его; подписка привязана к user_id из web-сессии), /api/web/push/vapid-key, POST/DELETE /api/web/push/subscription (только с сессией). Канал push в calendar-notifier рядом с Telegram: тот же выбор событий (важные USD, за 15 мин), свой ключ в журнале на (событие, подписка), чтобы рестарт не повторял; ответ 404/410 от push-сервиса → подписка удаляется. Дашборд: service worker (свой маленький sw.js или @angular/service-worker SwPush — выбрать и обосновать), переключатель в шапке подписывает/отписывает; при живой подписке вкладочный уведомитель IB-061 не дублирует (тот же tag уведомления — showNotification с tag заменяет; проверить вживую). Клик по уведомлению открывает дашборд. Ограничения: push работает только на https или localhost — записать в отчёте, что на будущем сервере нужен HTTPS (связь с задачей развёртывания). Готово: specs (выбор и дедуп по подписке, удаление по 410, контроллер с/без сессии), jest бота и npm test зелёные; вживую на слоте: подписаться в браузере, закрыть вкладку, тестовое событие через несколько минут → системное уведомление пришло; после рестарта бота не повторилось; отписка — больше не приходит. Без браузера — так и сказать.

title: TradFi-перпы в списке символов: металлы, нефть, газ, медь, SPY/QQQ (Binance, Bybit, OKX)

Сейчас их ликвидации уже пишутся (Binance !forceOrder@arr приходит по всем символам: за сутки XAGUSDT 76 / $2.47M, XAUUSDT 87 / $1.08M — больше, чем у многих монет), но /liquidations/events отдаёт [] (символа нет в symbols, IB-BUG-011), и в выборе символа их нет. Где торгуются (проверено координатором 2026-10-30 одним запросом списков инструментов): Binance USD-M XAUUSDT (onboard 2025-12-11) и XAGUSDT (2026-01-07), underlyingType COMMODITY, contractType TRADIFI_PERPETUAL; Bybit linear XAUUSDT, XAGUSDT; OKX XAU-USDT-SWAP, XAG-USDT-SWAP. Спота на Binance нет (binance_spot: null) — поэтому их и исключили в IB-003 (комментарий в universe.yaml); спотового CVD у них не будет — это нормально, не падать. Сделать: две записи в apps/insight-bot/config/universe.yaml (listed_perp — по первому бару в архиве data.binance.vision или onboardDate; coingecko_id: null, если схема позволяет, иначе обосновать; сопоставление Bybit/OKX проверить ценой, как в комментарии universe.yaml); переписать комментарий о фильтре (исключение больше не правило: TradFi-перпы добавляются руками по решению пользователя); проверить, что все пути с binance_spot = null и без coingecko_id работают (коллекторы, OI/LS-поллер, фандинг-бэкфилл трёх бирж, сводка /universe/summary, страница инструмента, рыночный контекст, features — где символ не крипта, не должен ронять расчёт); вес Binance в минуту от +2 символов в OI/LS-поллере и прочих опросах записать в комментарии. Готово: jest бота и npm test зелёные; вживую на слоте: XAUUSDT и XAGUSDT в выборе символа, свечи (perp), OI, фандинг, пузыри ликвидаций Binance/Bybit/OKX видны, /health без деградаций, в логе нет ошибок по этим символам. | Расширено 2026-10-30 (пользователь «да давай добавим»): кроме XAU/XAG добавить остальное сырьё Binance — CLUSDT (WTI), BZUSDT (Brent), NATGASUSDT, COPPERUSDT, XPTUSDT, XPDUSDT — и индексы SPYUSDT, QQQUSDT; для каждого найти пары на Bybit/OKX (CL есть на Bybit и OKX, XPT на OKX), сверить по цене. Акции поштучно не добавлять. Отдельно и явно проверить, что всё переживает отсутствие спота Binance (binance_spot null): сводка /universe/summary и выбор символа, страница инструмента (все панели, плитки «сейчас», CVD), расчёты (features, regime, derive, рыночный контекст) — по каждому пути spec или живая проверка, в отчёте таблицей.

title: Свечи с Bybit и форекс-символы Bybit (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY)
description: Пользователь 2026-10-30: свечи с Bybit — отдельной задачей, чтобы показывать форекс Bybit (EURUSDUSDT, GBPUSDUSDT, USDJPYUSDT), которого нет на Binance и OKX. Бриф: ~/.claude/jobs/0028abca/tmp/reports/dev-3-ib-bybit-candles.md (переиспользовать; номер миграции перепроверить). | ПЕРЕСМОТРЕНО 2026-10-31 (Архитектор): решение пользователя «только крипта, без форекса и индексов» (бриф member-access §1.3) снимает единственную причину задачи — форекс Bybit.
